verdicts.reviewer_notes: Second review. Re-fetched EUR-Lex CELEX:32024R1689. It confirms the signature date ('of 13 June 2024'), OJ publication on 12 July 2024, the 'In force' status, and consolidated versions dated 12/07/2024 and 27/07/2026. Re-fetched the consolidated Article 113 on the Commission AI Act Service Desk (https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-113). It says the Regulation enters into force 'on the twentieth day following that of its publication', so 12 July + 20 days = 1 August 2024. It sets general application from 2 August 2026. Chapters I and II apply from 2 February 2025, except Article 5(1)(ba)/(bb), 5(1a) and 5(1b), which apply from 2 December 2026. Annex III high-risk applies from 2 December 2027, Annex I from 2 August 2028, and Articles 102-110 from 27 July 2026. Re-fetched the 2026/1744 ELI page, which confirms entry into force on the third day after OJ publication on 24.7.2026, i.e. 27 July 2026. All earlier required changes have been applied: the 2024-08-01 in_force entry, the cleaned 2024-07-12 note, the summary sentence, and the consolidated schedule. Status in_force is correct. Tone is neutral. No duplicate: content/items/ and content/instruments/ contain no JSON files (Glob), and the slug appears once in the file. One remaining inaccuracy, so claim_matches_source fails. key_obligations[0] says 'GPAI, governance and penalties provisions from 2 August 2025' with no exception, but Article 113 applies Chapter XII 'with the exception of Article 101'. Article 101 (fines for GPAI model providers) therefore applies only from the general date of 2 August 2026. As written, readers could conclude the Commission could fine GPAI providers from August 2025. The previous review proposed this wording, and it was imprecise.
required_changes: key_obligations[0]: change 'GPAI, governance and penalties provisions from 2 August 2025' to 'GPAI, governance and penalties provisions from 2 August 2025 (except Article 101 fines on GPAI providers, which apply from 2 August 2026)'.

verdicts.reviewer_notes: Second review. Re-fetched https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744/oj/eng (EUR-Lex, primary). Verified the full title: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 of 8 July 2026, amending 2024/1689, 2018/1139 and 2023/1230, Digital Omnibus on AI. OJ L publication is 24.7.2026, and the act 'enters into force as a matter of urgency on the third day following that of its publication', i.e. 27 July 2026. All three timeline dates are correct. Status in_force is correct. Each key obligation was checked against the text. Annex III high-risk applies from 2 December 2027 and Annex I from 2 August 2028. Article 4 now requires providers and deployers to 'take measures to support the development of AI literacy'. New Article 5 prohibitions cover non-consensual intimate imagery and CSAM. The 2 December 2026 application date for those prohibitions is confirmed by consolidated Article 113 on the Commission AI Act Service Desk, which lists Article 5(1)(ba)/(bb), 5(1a) and 5(1b) from 2 December 2026. The EUR-Lex fetch summary was vague on this point, so I relied on the Service Desk text. SMEs and SMCs get simplified technical documentation (Article 11) and priority sandbox access. Article 4a extends special-category data processing for bias detection to deployers of high-risk systems and to providers and deployers of other AI systems and models, with safeguards. The earlier required changes (Article 5 application date, SMC wording) are applied correctly. No future-dated timeline stages. Tone is neutral. No duplicate (content/items/ and content/instruments/ empty; slug unique in file).

Second review. Re-fetched https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/contents-code-gpai (European Commission, primary, the issuing body). Verified: 'The code was published on July 10, 2025', which matches the summary and the single timeline entry. The page calls the code 'a voluntary tool'. The Transparency chapter (Model Documentation Form) and the Copyright chapter relate to Article 53. The Safety and Security chapter relates to Article 55 and applies only to providers of the most advanced (systemic-risk) models. Signatory count: the page lists exactly 21 names (AI Studio Delta, Aleph Alpha, Almawave, Amazon, Anthropic, Black Forest Labs, Bria AI, Cohere, Domyn, Dweve, Fastweb, Google, IBM, LINAGORA, Microsoft, Mistral AI, Open Hippo, OpenAI, Pleias, ServiceNow, WRITER). It then says separately: 'In addition, xAI signed up to the Safety and Security Chapter'. So '21 organisations ... signing the full code and xAI signing only the Safety and Security chapter' is accurate, and xAI is not double-counted. Status is now 'passed', consistent with the timeline and with a voluntary instrument. The earlier meta-commentary sentence has been removed. Tone is neutral. No duplicate.

Second review. Re-fetched https://www.admin.ch/gov/en/start/documentation/media-releases.msg-id-104110.html (Federal Council, primary). It confirms that on 12 February 2025 'Switzerland intends to ratify the Council of Europe Convention on Artificial Intelligence (AI) and to make the necessary amendments to Swiss law', and that 'Work will also continue on the regulation of AI in specific sectors such as healthcare and transport.' Re-fetched the newly cited https://www.bk.admin.ch/en/artificial-intelligence (Federal Chancellery, primary). It confirms that the FDJP with DETEC, the FDFA and other offices will 'draw up a bill on AI regulation to be submitted for consultation by the end of 2026', covering 'transparency, data protection, non-discrimination and supervision'. It also confirms the implementation plan for non-binding measures (industry solutions, voluntary commitment declarations) due by end of 2026, and that 'The Federal Chancellery has also maintained a contact point for the Federal Administration since 1 February 2026.' The earlier required changes are applied: the bk.admin.ch citation, the contact-point wording, the FDJP/DETEC/FDFA wording, removal of the process commentary, and the key_obligations[0] parenthetical. Both timeline dates match their sources. Status 'proposed' is the closest enum for a government decision with no bill yet. Tone is neutral. No duplicate. claim_matches_source still fails on a point the first review missed. key_obligations[1] says 'Sector-specific amendments rather than a horizontal AI law', and the summary ends 'No comprehensive AI act.' I asked for verbatim text on this from all three admin pages (the admin.ch release, bk.admin.ch/en/artificial-intelligence and bk.admin.ch/en/regulation). None of them says the Federal Council rejected a horizontal law. The admin.ch release says only that sector work 'will also continue'. The bk.admin.ch page describes a 'bill on AI regulation' with cross-cutting topics (transparency, data protection, non-discrimination, supervision), which reads as at least partly cross-sector. It states only that 'there is not yet any overarching legislation that deals specifically with AI'. 'Rather than a horizontal AI law' is therefore an inference that the cited sources do not support. 'No comprehensive AI act.' is supportable only as a statement of the current position, not as a policy choice.
required_changes: key_obligations[1]: replace 'Sector-specific amendments rather than a horizontal AI law' with 'Continued work on AI regulation in specific sectors such as healthcare and transport (Federal Council, 12 February 2025)'.
Summary: replace the fragment 'No comprehensive AI act.' with 'According to the Federal Chancellery, there is not yet any overarching legislation in Switzerland that deals specifically with AI.'
